note: Per-episode archive-title queries. The unattended queue used ONE generic list for every episode (prison / jail / police / courtroom ...), which is why a British Post Office IT scandal ended up carrying American patrol footage, a neon HOTEL sign and a rice paddy: the generic terms matched, the subject did not. Each episode now asks for what its own story contains.

surfside.note: Champlain Towers South, Surfside FL, June 2021: a 12-storey oceanfront condo collapses at 1:22am. 2018 engineer report on garage/pool-deck damage, years of board fights over the repair bill, 98 dead. BANNED SUBJECT MATTER (design owner, 2026-08-02, binding): this film does NOT depict the collapse, the rubble, rescue or firefighting operations, ambulances, casualties or memorial-of-the-dead imagery. The queries debris / demolition / excavator / emergency / ambulance / burning candle / smoke building / abandoned building were removed on that ground and must not come back. The pool is the BUILDING and the DECISION: concrete, columns, the garage, the pool deck, water, balconies, corridors, drawings, meetings, letters and money, the ocean and the night.
surfside._why: Terms are ANDed SUBSTRING matches against human-written archive titles, so every query here was probed against the ledger before it was written (2026-08-02). The previous list was written as descriptive phrases -- apartment building exterior, cracked concrete, rebar rust corrosion, memorial flowers fence, missing person poster, board meeting -- and 37 of its 38 queries returned ZERO rows. Do not add bare broad words either: rust matches frustrated, surf matches surface, ski matches asking, pier matches copier, sea wall matches wallpaper. The archive has no courtroom, gavel, judge, invoice, envelope or corrosion footage left that another episode has not already taken. Subtropical coastal only: nothing that invites snow, alps, ski, winter, neon sci-fi tunnels or foreign landmarks.

flowers.note: Winona, Mississippi 1996: four people shot in a furniture store; six trials; jury selection. Terms are ANDed against the ledger TITLE, so they are written as phrases the archive actually uses: single generic words (street, court, farm, church) returned Berlin, a basketball court, a rice paddy and a Montenegrin cliff chapel, and 115 of 204 clips were rejected on sight. Nothing here may invite snow, mountains, coastline, foreign streets and signage, modern open-plan offices or law-firm advertising.

postoffice.note: England 1999-2024: Horizon accounting software, village sub-postmasters, private prosecutions. Visual QC on 2026-08-02 rejected 152 clips: American patrol cars and US small-town aerials, US Supreme Court steps, dollar/zloty/peso money, gavels (English courts have none), Anonymous-mask hackers, labs and hospitals, law-firm adverts, modern smartphone fintech. Do not ask for police, courtroom, judge, gavel, banknotes, server room, spreadsheet or office desk here -- those generic terms are what pulled all of it in.

hyatt.note: EP69 Kansas City Hyatt Regency walkways, 1978-1988 USA. Registers R1-R20 and the terms themselves come from the episode's own measured plan, EP69_hyatt_FOOTAGE_PLAN.v001.md s4: each term is one the plan measured a USABLE count for after licence, title-block, rip-signature, on-disk, size, cross-episode and 1920x1080 screens -- not a director's phrase. Five terms the plan measured as actively misleading are deliberately ABSENT even though their hit counts are high: 'plant' (89, botany), 'rig' (60, the word 'bright'), 'nut' (27, doughnuts; top hit is a police clip and 'police' is forbidden), 'cine' (62, 'medicine'/'cinematic') and 'sign' (270, signage carries readable text that places the shot elsewhere). 'people' (410) and 'architect' (424) are also absent: the first floods the people lane with modern crowds and the second returns European civic architecture, which s6 rule 7 bars. NO QUERY TERM IS A forbidden_subjects WORD -- check_spec_satisfied matches those word-wise against the staged FILENAME, so a title carrying collapse/rubble/rescue/police/child/hyatt is an automatic build failure, and this episode is a structural-collapse case where reaching for that imagery is exactly the defamatory cut (EP60 surfside staged 31 of them). Period is the binding risk and no machine measures it: era_setting is 1978-1988 and the steel, drafting and construction registers on this shelf are dominated by 2015-2024 footage, so footage_review_required is true and every clip is judged on frames before it is copied.

pinto.note: EP68 the Ford Pinto / Grimshaw v. Ford. USA 1968-1981 (Southern California; Elkhart County and Winamac, Indiana; Ford engineering interiors; Washington DC). Queries are verbatim from episodes/_planning/EP68_pinto_FOOTAGE_PLAN.v001.md s4: 623 queries were measured against the ledger over two rounds, 470 table rows returned at least one unused >=1920x1080 clip, and those are 465 distinct queries -- kept here ordered by register (R1 the car .. R20 dusk) and by measured supply inside each register. Director's words returned zero where supplier's words returned hundreds (PD_CANON s10): `courthouse` 0 / `arch` 468, `grey sky` 0 / `clouds` 500, `crash test` 0 / `hit` 641. A HIT COUNT IS NOT A SUPPLY COUNT, and three of those wins are traps: `hit` is mostly waves on rocks, `arch` is European cathedrals and Asian temples, and this film may show no collision at all. CORRECTED 2026-08-12: the sentence that stood here claimed the 124 forbidden_subjects in episode_spec were applied to candidate titles before staging. NO CODE DID THAT, and 106 of the 807 candidates this query set produced carried a forbidden term as a whole word in their own ledger title (drone 26, burning 14, beach 11, smoke 10, fire 5, police 4). They are applied now, for real, by stage_footage_by_title.forbidden_hit at selection and by prestage_footage_review.filter_forbidden on the candidate list -- check_spec_satisfied matches them word-wise against the staged filename, so a survivor is an automatic build failure after the render. CONSEQUENCE, AND IT NEEDS AN OWNER DECISION: 20 of the 465 queries below ARE forbidden subjects (ash, fire, smoke, burn, burning, flame, crash, bonfire, black smoke, campfire, wreck, candle flame, soot, smoke rising, ember, accident, car crash, wrecked car, smoke slow, hourglass), so assert_queries_clean now REFUSES to run this set until either those queries or the spec change. Do not resolve it by weakening forbidden_subjects. The four registers the archive cannot supply at all (typed paper, the underside of a car, an American courthouse, and 1968-1981 itself) are carried by generated plates R001-R080 and by no query here.

wronghouse.note: REWRITTEN 2026-08-21 after measuring what the SHIPPED episodes actually cut. The first query set for this slug asked for the case's own furniture -- front doors, mailboxes, courthouses -- and 5 of 5 sampled contact sheets came back Copenhagen, a Japanese pagoda, the Black Forest and 3D chroma-key CGI. That was the wrong question. Counting the factory clips that openfields, marmet, greene and hyatt REALLY used shows what this channel's footage lane is for: clouds 59, forest 50, trees 37, time-lapse 30, sunset 31, leaves 25, landscape 25, field 23, autumn 21. It is CONNECTIVE TISSUE -- weather, season, light, time passing between the commissioned plates -- not a reconstruction of the events. The plates carry the case; the shelf carries the breathing room. Measured against the rebuilt ledger with scripts/measure_shelf_for_episode.py, counting only license_decision 'pd' and subtracting any hit whose filename carries one of this episode's 209 forbidden words: nature 1393, landscape 718, road 646, forest 516, sky 482, clouds 430, sunset 426, walking 316, street 313, trees 304, night 265, river 265. The supply is there; the earlier 'the shelf cannot dress EP70' conclusion was a wrong query, not a missing shelf. Every clip still needs a human to open the contact sheet -- EP71's own spec measured a 70-clip sample at 50% off-register, and this shelf's labels were 40% wrong even when it had a ledger.

oroville.note: EP71 Oroville, v002 query set, 2026-08-20 23:xx. THE PREVIOUS 101-TERM SET WAS READ ON CONTACT SHEETS AND FAILED: 56 candidates judged, 3 usable (5%), against the episode's own already-bad 50% precision sample. Full record in runs/qc/oroville_footage_review.v001.md. The failure was structural, not accidental -- the subject-bearing registers were each carried by one generic word that is not the subject (`animal` 422 for cattle returned a snail, an owl, a labrador and a cartoon dog; `mountain` 228 for foothills returned the Alps; `architecture` 135 for civic returned a university library). Those registers are REMOVED from the shelf entirely and are dressed by plates O001-O118, which is what they were always for. What remains is the four registers where PLACE DOES NOT MATTER: an overcast sky, a water surface, an anonymous hand, a road surface. A cloud filmed anywhere is a cloud in Butte County; a cow filmed anywhere is not a Butte County cow. That distinction is the whole content of this revision. `earth` (76) is excluded because it returns the planet from orbit, and `walk`/`walking` (694) because they return identifiable faces, which the people lane forbids. Every term below was measured against the ledger rebuilt 2026-08-20 and screened against all 131 forbidden_subjects. TOP-UP 2026-08-21: 20 more terms in the same four place-neutral families, because the first pass staged 38 and check_episode_inputs floors the pool at 40. `rock` measured 150 and was REFUSED anyway -- it returns cliffs, coast and mountain faces, which is the wide-shot failure this revision exists to avoid; `sand` (26) refused for the same reason, the spec bans the beach. A fifth family was opened for paper/notebook/pen: tabletop documents are as place-neutral as a raindrop and the film has document beats the plates only partly cover.

itaewon.note: Itaewon, Yongsan-gu, Seoul, 29 October 2022: a sloping alley beside the Hamilton Hotel, about 50 m long, 5 m wide at the top and 3.2 m at the bottom, fills from both ends on the first Halloween after the mask mandate lifted. Eleven 112 calls between 18:34 and 22:11; officers sent to four. 159 dead. BANNED SUBJECT MATTER (binding, episode_spec.forbidden_subjects, 63 terms): this film NEVER depicts the crush or anything implying one -- no body, no fallen person, no CPR, no stretcher, no blood, no covered figure -- and never a crowd at crush density. The alley appears in three states only: empty, ordinarily busy, after. No memorial, no candles, no flowers, no funeral. No gavel: Korean courts do not use one. WRONG COUNTRY IS THE OTHER FAILURE: Tokyo, Shibuya, Shanghai, Hong Kong, Bangkok, Times Square, London and generic European streets are all blocked, as are kana and Chinese shopfronts. Korea, or unreadable. Festival, parade, carnival, concert and stadium crowds are blocked: they read as fun.

morandi.note: EP76 Morandi, v001 query set, MEASURED 2026-08-21 before it was written. THE HEADLINE FINDING IS POSITIVE, which is the opposite of EP75 and worth saying plainly: this shelf CAN carry most of this film. The registers this story needs -- an ordinary car on an ordinary elevated road, a working container port, and hands on paper in an office -- are the shelf's strongest holdings. Measured: road traffic 303, car traffic 265, urban traffic 102, highway traffic 117, night road 53, tunnel 68; dock 46, shipping 34, cargo ship 33, shipyard 23, container ship 9; office desk 78, typing 80, writing 66, keyboard 62, notebook 39, hands writing 37, hands typing 28, documents 12, library 111; timelapse 906, fog 154, particle 98, cloudscape 79, dust 52. WHAT THE SHELF DOES NOT HAVE is the film's own texture, and that is what plates V001-V120 were written for: concrete 20, rust 19, warehouse 19, industrial 20, excavator 45 -- and then corrosion 1, rebar 1, girder 1, viaduct 1, scaffolding 1, cracked wall 1, guardrail 1, roadworks 1, hillside 1, shutters 1. There is no weathered prestressed concrete on this shelf and there is no Ligurian street on it either. EXCLUDED BY SUBSTRING TRAP, measured by reading what came back, do not re-add: `port` (554) is mostly transPORTation, PORTugal and PORTal; `rain` (491) is mostly tRAINing, railway and 'money raining' which is itself a forbidden subject; `paper` (914) is mostly newsPAPER and 'beautiful wallPAPER' flags and landscapes, and a legible newspaper is a fabricated_record; `file` (30) is proFILE and 'video file'; `toll` (6) is entirely aTOLL, tropical reef; `beam` (30) is a gymnast's balance beam and sunbeams, with zero structural beams; `stamp` (12) is passport stamps and rubber stamps WITH READABLE TEXT; `hand` (807) and `hands` (723) are people eating pizza and dancing, not paperwork -- use `hands writing` and `hands typing`. EXCLUDED BY SUBJECT, and this is the one that matters most here: `italy` (84) returns VENICE GONDOLAS, TUSCAN CYPRESS AVENUES and the DOLOMITES -- precisely the holiday-Italy register this episode's own era_setting and forbidden_subjects bar. The most obvious search term for an Italian film is the most dangerous term in it. CONDITIONAL, kept but never taken on the count alone: `crane` (43) mixes port and construction cranes with CRANE BIRDS; `railway` (52) is Japan, Switzerland, Disneyland and snow; `corridor` (55) is largely sci-fi and horror 3D tunnels; `city street` (230) shows Mexico City, Bogota and Basel, and a visible foreign street is the same class of error as a US route shield; `cloudscape` (79) is heavy with drone sunsets and golden hour, which this film bars outright; `construction` (140) mixes welders and excavators with birds and cathedrals. footage_review_required is TRUE and the factory shelf's labels are known to be wrong, so nothing here enters a cut before a person opens a labelled contact sheet.
registers: the ordinary drive -- a car on an elevated road, traffic at deck level, a tunnel portal, wet asphalt. This is the film's subject ('the thing you do without thinking') and the shelf's strongest holding. Place must not be legible: no US route shield, no right-hand drive, no visibly foreign street furniture
a working container port -- cranes, docks, a cargo ship, a shipyard. Genoa is a port, and this is the ONE place-register the shelf can actually supply
hands and paper at a desk -- typing, writing, a notebook, documents, an office desk, a library shelf. Carries the whole of ACT_3 and ACT_4, at a scale where no face resolves
sky and texture -- fog, haze, cloud, dust, grain, particle, timelapse. Flat and grey only; golden hour and drone sunsets are barred by the film's three light states
the valley floor under the bridge -- warehouse, industrial, excavator, freight. Thin on this shelf and supplemented by plates
